# Jennifer McDonald

# Board Member

![](/media/uploads/2026/08/District4JenniferMcDonald-square-enhanced.png)

- Approved a policy that “supports and encourages an environment that fosters independent and critical thought, including the studying and teaching of issues which may be considered controversial or divisive. Atlanta Public Schools students and teachers have the following rights: To study and teach any controversial or divisive issue that has political, economic, or social significance in an age- and developmentally- appropriate manner.” and “To form and express opinions on controversial or divisive issues without fear of retaliation.”

![](/media/uploads/2026/08/Mcdonald1.png)

![](/media/uploads/2026/08/Mcdonald2.png)

- In a [candidate questionnaire](https://web.archive.org/web/20260610045908/https:/civicatlanta.org/voteatl/2025-school-board-candidate-responses#jennifer-mcdonald) McDonald said, “We as a district have acknowledged disproportionate discipline practices, particularly affecting Black students and students with disabilities, and we have implemented initiatives to address the school-to-prison pipeline. Data has shown that Black students in APS are suspended and expelled at a significantly higher rate than their white peers. We have revised its Student Code of Conduct to provide a more progressive and tiered approach to discipline.”
- [McDonald said](https://web.archive.org/web/20260610045908/https:/civicatlanta.org/voteatl/2025-school-board-candidate-responses#jennifer-mcdonald), “I advocate for ongoing training for all staff on implicit bias,”
